reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a sandwich-frontrunning bot with a claimed 7000% monthly return and instructs viewers to visit a site, buy, download, and deploy the software. It presents rapid profit extraction, daily profits, and simple setup as accessible to non-developers. The warning about impersonators directing users to fund a Remix smart contract does not verify the advertised returns, software performance, or transaction outcomes.

HOW TO GET STARTED. 1. Visit https://www.mevengine.com 2. Buy and Download Your Sandwich Bot 3. Deploy on Your node with Our Simple Guide.
The sandwich bot frontruns a targeted transaction with a higher fee and extracts the profits from the transaction.
Now as a non developer individual, you can out perform and Out trade the regular M E V Sandwich Bot and make daily profit with simple setup.

opening.argument: Judge, the headline's return figure deserves scrutiny, but it is not the whole message. The description explicitly warns viewers about impersonators and about being directed to fund a Remix smart contract. That warning distinguishes buying software from sending funds into an unverified contract. The record does not show a viewer being told to deposit trading capital with the seller, nor does it show a completed transaction or a realized return. Read the profit language as an aggressive product claim that needs verification, not, by itself, proof of a deceptive transfer scheme.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The headline supplies a claimed return, not evidence that anyone received it. The buy-and-deploy steps identify a software purchase; they do not direct viewers to fund the Remix contract the description expressly warns against. Calling that warning insufficient to verify performance is fair, but lack of verification alone does not establish the warned-against funding conduct.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warning concerns impersonation and one way of funding a contract; it does not qualify the video's own return claim. The seller still urges viewers to buy and deploy its bot, while presenting daily profit with simple setup as available to non-developers. No achieved return is needed to recognize that the solicitation rests on extraordinary, unverified profit claims.

Make 7000% Monthly With MevEngine SANDWICH FRONTRUNNING MEVBOT
Now as a non developer individual, you can out perform and Out trade the regular M E V Sandwich Bot and make daily profit with simple setup.

opening.argument: Judge, there is substantive technical explanation here. The narration describes the proposed sequence: a bot pays a higher fee to get ahead of a targeted transaction, then back-runs it. It also discusses detection features and deployment on additional blockchain networks. Those details give a viewer a way to understand what the advertised tool is supposed to do. The record does not show the steps of a completed trade or prove that the described system works; the narrower reading is a technology-focused explanation containing promotional claims, not evidence that the claimed profits were obtained.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited description of how a bot would front-run a transaction is an explanation of a proposed mechanism, not a demonstration that this bot executed it or earned the headline return. The closing download invitation makes the presentation promotional, but promotion can coexist with technical explanation. The opening conflates what the narration says the tool does with proof of an actual outcome.

citations.quote: The sandwich bot frontruns a targeted transaction with a higher fee and extracts the profits from the transaction.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical details serve the sales pitch: the narration ties the proposed mechanism to maximum profit, and the description tells viewers to buy and deploy the bot. The title promises a monthly return. The absence of a completed trade does not turn these assertions into a neutral demonstration; it leaves the promoted results unverified.

citations.quote: To ensure maximum profit, the Sandwich Bot is also able to back run the same transaction at the same time for maximum profit.
Buy and Download Your Sandwich Bot 3. Deploy on Your node with Our Simple Guide.
Make 7000% Monthly With MevEngine SANDWICH FRONTRUNNING MEVBOT

opening.argument: Judge, the concrete transaction requested is a purchase of downloadable software followed by deployment on the buyer's own node. The description presents the tool as an alternative to consulting an unknown developer. That is an identifiable product-and-service proposition, even if its performance claims warrant skepticism. The supplied material does not show a request for account credentials, a downline recruitment requirement, or an instruction to transfer investment funds to the seller. Evaluate the advertised return critically, but do not infer those additional mechanisms from a software sales pitch alone.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening establishes a site, a purchase instruction, and profit claims. It does not establish a deposit into the seller's custody, a credential request, or a realized return. Those distinctions matter: a buyer-operated software product can be marketed with exaggerated claims without the record proving a separate funds-transfer scheme.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The lack of a credential request or seller-held deposit does not answer the concern here. The product being sold is explicitly linked to a 7000% monthly claim, and the narration tells non-developers they can make daily profit with simple setup. The purchase instruction is the solicitation; calling it ordinary commerce does not validate the promised results.
